observed_trace_validation.scope: Observed candidate availability and target choice only; no measured alternate-policy speedup or source-content age
observed_trace_validation.continuity_scope: Successful projection submissions only; schema 1/2 does not record every render attempt. Target gaps establish only compatibility with intervening renders, not their count or outcome.
observed_trace_validation.warning: Higher frame ID or target is not proof of a newer application scene or physical display time

limitations: Application frame identity is not a simulation or input epoch.
Host monotonic callbacks are not photon or client clock times.
Accepted compositor input is not proof of encoded delivery.
Projection target matching does not establish layer ownership when targets coincide.
Trace adds atomic and clock-read overhead; do not use for promotion.

assumptions: Only exact complete recorded histories or actually retained pairs at observed selections are available.
Deadlines, publication/receive timestamps, source identity, skipped attempts and feedback are frozen.
At most one advancing wire ID per observed deadline; frame IDs strictly advance and source targets do not regress.
Warm-start ownership, closest-target guards and successor reservation are relaxed; waiting and repeats cost nothing.
A larger target envelope is a diagnostic relaxation, not permission to submit an unqualified future-predicted pose.
Removing the target ceiling does not introduce frames outside the exact recorded snapshots.
The maximum-count and maximum-under-threshold objectives can select different paths.
A lower optimistic age bound is not an attainable selector or live cadence result.
Source IDs identify latched application generations, not distinct simulation epochs or optical freshness.
Host source timestamps are never subtracted from client timestamps.
